title: Legal AI Engineer (Berlin or Leipzig)
description:
Description

Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.

Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.

Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.


Your mission

Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.


Your profile

The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant: a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.


Why us?

  • Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
  • No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.
  • We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.
  • Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).
  • Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.

title: Project Planner (Data Centres/Buildings/High-tech/Infrastructure) -  Frankfurt/Berlin/Munich (Hybrid)
description:
Are you a bit tired of the standard, old-fashioned way of doing things in the construction industry? 
Do you get deep satisfaction from making things run more efficiently using a good dose of common sense and maybe a bit of technology? 
Have you always cared about the importance of proper planning and the connection between the schedule and the real, day-to-day delivery of the job? 
Have you ever wanted to work a bit more flexibly but still be hands-on in construction and improving the industry? 
Sounds like a dream. Well, it isn’t. It’s quite real! Read on. 
____________________________________________________________
We are Laminar Projects!
 
If you’ve already heard about us, you’re probably reading this because you’re tired of the typical, chaotic ways of doing things in construction. But in case you haven’t, we’re a high-end project management consultancy and tech developer with a focus on upgrading the way construction projects are delivered.
 
Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. (Check out our short film about it.)
We bring transparency and control to projects through a pragmatic mix of the latest tech, our own processes, and a big dose of common sense. We then take our deep understanding of these projects and we invest heavily into developing the digital solutions that anyone can use to deliver their projects better. (Check out Shape, our construction management tech, to see what we’re doing.)
 
The core of all this is our true secret sauce: our people. We only recruit the very best, both in capability and personality. We’re deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that’s optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People who join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined. (Read more about our vision and missions.)
 
This approach has allowed us to grow from just two people in 2017 to over 220 today. We have a stable, repeat client base across infrastructure and complex building projects in the UK and internationally, and we’re still growing fast. Joining us isn’t just some “job”. It’s a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life. There are many diverse and interesting challenges available. It’s up to you to guide yourself into whichever areas you’re most interested – we’ll enable it. 
 
(Get to know us better by watching a few more of our videos.)
 
Core values for a good life
 
A life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships and challenging yourself to create a positive impact, so our values reflect the four levels of relationships that each of us has:
 
- Grow yourself – your relationship with yourself 
- Care about people – your relationship with others around you 
- Execute to greatness – your relationship with your team 
- Build civilisation – your relationship with humanity and the world 
 
We enshrined our values in our vision:
 
We exist so that everyone in our team can flourish in a high-impact community that:
 
- Connects us with meaningful relationships 
- Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans 
- Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures 
 
By first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world.
 
And enable the achievement of our vision through our two missions:
 
- To fully digitalise the construction of human civilisation 
- To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society 
____________________________________________________________
The Role 
 
Purpose of the role 
 
You’ll be enhancing the delivery of the most complex and interesting projects in the world through the power of project planning to the very highest standards. You’ll devise strategies and tactics to improve the way the project is delivered. You’ll translate this knowledge into a logic-linked plan and analyse it using planning software. Then you’ll use the plan to help the teams understand what to prioritise. 
 
Your team 
 
This role is part of our Project Management Consultancy team which focuses on:
 
- Understanding what the real problems of projects are 
- Implementing the best solutions to those problems 
- Developing scalable best practices, tools and technology 
 
More specifically, you’ll be part of our Project Planning Team, who are industry leaders in the planning of complex construction projects. Your initial leader will be one of our planning discipline directors.
 
Your top three objectives 
 
1. To make construction projects deliver to near perfection 
2. To create scalable and repeatable solutions to common problems 
3. To develop yourself and everyone around you 
 
Your top five responsibilities 
 
1. Own the plan: Own the project plan for one or more projects and ensure that the project is working to it effectively. Ensure delays are mitigated and managed commercially 
2. Own the outcome: You're responsible for putting in your best effort to ensure the project team’s understanding and focus on the plan – no matter how stubborn they are 
3. Report and inform: Provide simple, actionable reports to stakeholders at all levels that help them deliver their part of the project more efficiently and effectively 
4. Make scalable solutions: Develop scalable and repeatable best practices and tools in collaboration with the team so that long-term impact is achieved 
5. Develop everyone: Maximise the development of your team personally and professionally and educate our clients to improve as well  
 
You must have:
 
- A construction engineering background: You have at least 2+ years of experience on construction projects, experience in project planning both software and principles, as well as decent Excel skills, and a strong interest in data
- Communication skills: You’re proficient in written and verbal English and have the charisma and influence to get construction people to do new things and take the best approach 
- Leadership capabilities: You lead yourself proactively and lead others by asking the right questions and challenging them 
- Impact: You have a track record of making projects and organisations better beyond just doing the basics – implementing scalable, repeatable solutions that had a significant positive impact 
 
Laminar isn’t the place for you if any of the following is true: 
 
- You want an easy, chilled-out role without much challenge 
- You like to be the smartest person in the room 
- You don’t like continuously receiving honest candid feedback 
- You prefer to do your own thing rather than work with a team
____________________________________________________________
Frequently Asked Questions 
 
What kinds of projects would I be working on?
It’s common for people to be exposed to several projects in their first year with us. You’ll work on some of the most complex and interesting environments in the world. We’ve delivered over 100 data centres internationally, many of them fast-tracked and multi-package. Our teams have supported flagship infrastructure programmes like HS2 through integrated planning and digital delivery, contributed to over $30bn in power generation and transmission projects, and played a key role in the development of high-containment labs and R&D campuses for some of the world’s most advanced industrial and life sciences clients. You might find yourself working in sectors such as data centres, infrastructure (including defense, rail, and highways), high tech (such as advanced manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and semiconductors), or complex building projects. These aren’t hands-off assignments. They’re dynamic, hands-on environments designed for people who want to be challenged. We bring back the lessons from every project to help our team grow and deliver the highest levels of value. (Check out our case stories.) 
 
Who are our clients?
Major owners/operators and main contractors with project values between £1m and £1bn+ globally. 
 
Where would I be working?
One week you might be working from home. The next, you might travel to the site to meet the construction teams and help organise them. Maybe you’ll pop into our London office for a workshop or a beer. Maybe you’ll fly out to exotic (and sometimes not!) locations in Europe or the Middle East to visit clients. It really depends on what you want to get involved in and what fits with your life. 
 
How does what I do connect with the long-term impact on the construction industry? 
You’re tasked with understanding and solving common problems. We don’t want to reinvent the wheel every time, so you’ll be responsible for documenting new solutions and evolving ones we’ve developed. This goes into our knowledge repository, which we’re going to open source to the industry. 
 
The knowledge you capture will be used by us to build new products. You’ll constantly test those products in the field, so we can rapidly iterate and improve them for anyone in the industry to use. 
 
____________________________________________________________
 
Benefits
 
The standard stuff: 
 
- Bonus Scheme. As a permanent member of the team, you’ll share in our success. Our annual bonus is designed to reward both the now and the future - with a flexible mix of cash and high-growth equity that you choose. Bonuses are discretionary and based on performance 
- Professional body membership. One fee covered per year - so you can stay connected to your field and develop your craft 
 
The life-changing stuff:
 
- In-house coaching. Regular 1:1 coaching sessions, fully confidential, to help you navigate challenges, build self-awareness, and grow intentionally - professionally and as a human being
- Equity upside. As we grow, you grow. Our generous equity scheme is especially powerful for those who stay with us on our journey. You help us build the future - and own a piece of it
- Flexible working. Work where it makes sense - most of our team works from home, visiting sites or clients regularly. We care about outcomes, not clock-ins
- Relentless development. Our goal is for every year here to be worth five years of development anywhere else. You’ll get a coach, a mentor, honest feedback, and a culture that challenges you to keep levelling up
____________________________________________________________
 
Important! Applying properly
 
We get thousands of applications so please write us a letter as part of your application explaining:
 
- Why you want to join us 
- What you’ll bring to the team 
 
We aren't a giant, faceless corporation; we really care about the people who want to join our team, so your letter will be read carefully. After that, we’ll reach out to you to schedule a casual conversation to help you get to know us a bit better and tell us a bit about yourself. A couple of technical and personal assessments follow to understand your capability based on our own development matrix.  
 
This is to ensure that when you join, you’re starting at the right level of responsibility.

Working with Operations, Supply Chain, suppliers, customers and international Quality functions, it drives effective controls, audit preparation and corrective action.   • Investigate complaints and non-conformities, driving effective corrective actions.
  • Manage supplier quality assessments, approval documentation and issue resolution.

  • Practical experience supporting QS, BIO and GQB certification requirements.
  • Formal HACCP or internal/lead auditor training relevant to food safety and quality.

title: Independent Consultant - Sustainable Bio-Materials & Regulatory Compliance
description:
RSB – Roundtable on Sustainable Biomaterials is a global, multi-stakeholder organisation dedicated to driving the truly sustainable development of the bioeconomy. Frequently recognised as an industry leader in supply chain sustainability, RSB applies its best-in-class sustainability framework across sectors including aviation, chemicals, materials, and shipping.

Our small, dedicated team operates remotely from countries around the world, working collaboratively with a diverse base of member organisations, industry partners, and policymakers. For more information, please visit www.rsb.org.

Purpose of This Call

RSB now invites eligible firms and individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services described below. This Call for Expressions of Interest is not yet linked to a specific project or immediate assignment. RSB is building a pre-approved External Consultant Roster: a qualified pool of selected specialists and organisations that will be called upon for project-based work for the next 2-3 years.

We are primarily seeking to engage consultancy firms, agencies, and other established organisations, providers that can offer dedicated capacity, depth of expertise, and continuity across assignments. At the same time, we warmly welcome expressions of interest from independent consultants and other individual specialists whose qualifications and experience match the profiles sought. Throughout this document, “Consultant” refers to both firms and individuals unless stated otherwise.

Consultants accepted onto the roster will complete a brief onboarding process to become familiar with RSB’s systems, ways of working, and sustainability framework, so that engagements can begin efficiently when a relevant need is identified. When a specific project or capacity gap emerges, RSB will contact roster members whose profile best matches the assignment, share a defined scope of work, and invite them to submit a proposal.

Inclusion on the roster is an expression of readiness and fit and not a guarantee of immediate work or remuneration.

The Services

The Sustainable Bio-Materials & Regulatory Compliance Consultant will provide regulatory compliance and sustainability assessment expertise for bio-based materials, sustainable fuels, feedstocks and related value chains. Consultants in this profile support RSB Advisory Services with the expert practical interpretation of regulatory frameworks, such as EU RED, CORSIA and relevant voluntary certification requirements, including their GHG calculation methodologies. They support feedstock eligibility, low-ILUC considerations, sustainability-risk screening, voluntary scheme benchmarking and compliance gap identification.

Role purpose: To provide RSB with flexible, project-based technical capacity for assessing whether bio-based materials, fuels, feedstocks and supply chains meet applicable regulatory and voluntary sustainability requirements. The role helps RSB and its clients translate complex rules into defensible assessments, calculations and compliance pathways, particularly where GHG data quality, feedstock eligibility, certification readiness or regulatory interpretation are central to the assignment.

Full or partial coverage: Applicants are eligible whether they wish to cover the full scope or only a clearly defined subset of the technical areas and task requirements described below (partial coverage), based on their knowledge, skills and capabilities. Partial coverage applicants are encouraged to submit their candidacy as well.

Confidentiality: Due to non-disclosure and confidentiality commitments within RSB Advisory Services, specific project-related work cannot be attached to or disclosed in this call.

Key Responsibilities

•    Contribute to narrowing and confirming the scope, system boundaries and methodological approach for assessments under EU RED, CORSIA, RSB or other relevant regulatory and voluntary sustainability frameworks.

•    Review third-party-supplied GHG inventory data, apply consistency and plausibility checks, validate assumptions, clean data, identify missing or unreliable data, and propose defensible proxies or literature-based values where appropriate.

•    Support or perform GHG calculations and carbon-intensity assessments using relevant or pre-defined methodologies and tools, including the RSB GHG Calculator where applicable.

•    Prepare clear GHG, LCA or sustainability assessment reports using agreed templates, including methodology, assumptions, data-quality notes, result presentation and interpretation.

•    Provide support for the technical understanding of sustainable bio-material pathways and low-ILUC risk considerations under EU RED, CORSIA, RSB or equivalent requirements.

•    Support regulatory and voluntary-scheme gap analyses by participating in the documentation of benchmarking requirements, identifying, verifying or validating compliance risks, and reviewing third-party organisational documentation against criteria (met, not met or not applicable).

•    Review certification-readiness documentation under RSB guidance, including evidence related to feedstock origin, traceability, chain of custody, sustainability criteria and GHG claims.

•    Support the interpretation of policy or regulatory requirements for specific feedstocks, technologies, products or markets by providing supporting data and literature reviews, and translate findings into practical compliance options in line with the applicable standard requirements.

•    Support the development or refinement of methodologies, blueprints and decision tools for innovative sustainability assessments involving bio-based materials, fuels, chemicals or emerging feedstock pathways.

Requirements

Essential (all applicants, firms and individuals, must meet these criteria):

•    Strong written and spoken English proficiency.

•    Ability to maintain regular availability overlapping with CET working hours of a minimum of 4 hours per day.

•    Proven output/delivery track record in your area of expertise.

•    Full compliance with all applicable local laws and regulations, including tax and social security obligations, and legal authorisation to perform consultancy services in the country of residence or operation.

•    Strong collaboration and communication skills, the ability to operate autonomously, and a proactive approach to communicating progress, risks, and opportunities in a clear and constructive manner.

•    Self-sufficiency in a remote and fully digital working environment with reliable internet connectivity. Video calls and collaborative tools will be used for coordination.

 

Specific to this profile:

•    Proven hands-on experience applying EU RED, CORSIA, RSB or equivalent GHG and sustainability methodologies in client, certification, policy or project-development contexts.

•    Working knowledge of at least one major voluntary sustainability certification scheme, preferably RSB, ISCC or another scheme relevant to biofuels, SAF, biomass or bio-based materials.

•    Demonstrated ability to assess feedstock eligibility, GHG data quality, certification readiness or regulatory compliance for specific products, pathways or supply chains.

•    Ability to work independently with limited onboarding, document assumptions transparently and flag uncertainty, data gaps and compliance risks.

•    Strong written English and effective reporting skills for technical and non-technical audiences.

•    Strong communication skills and comfort working with client-provided data under confidentiality constraints.

•    CET ±5 hours time-zone compatibility, unless otherwise agreed for a specific assignment.

 

For firms / agencies:

•    Ability to assign appropriately qualified personnel to assignments and to ensure continuity of delivery, including cover for absences.

•    Confirmation that the named individuals proposed for RSB assignments meet the essential criteria above.

Desirable (will strengthen your Expression of Interest):

•    Working knowledge of the RSB standard and certification system in particular, or of ISCC.

•    Hands-on experience using the RSB GHG Calculator.

•    Experience developing or refining methodologies, blueprints or decision tools for emerging feedstock pathways, bio-based materials, fuels or chemicals.

Indicative Outputs (may include but are not limited to):
Specific deliverables, estimated time input, and project duration will be clarified in the Terms of Reference (TOR) issued to shortlisted roster members when a project need is identified.

•    Scoping notes defining system boundaries and the methodological approach for an assessment

•    GHG data review and validation notes (plausibility checks, data gaps, proposed proxies or literature values)

•    GHG calculations and carbon-intensity assessments (including RSB GHG Calculator outputs)

•    GHG, LCA or sustainability assessment reports based on agreed templates

•    Feedstock eligibility and low-ILUC risk assessments

•    Regulatory and voluntary-scheme benchmarking and gap analyses

•    Certification-readiness reviews and evidence/documentation checks

•    Policy and regulatory interpretation notes and literature reviews with practical compliance options

Methodologies, blueprints and decision tools for innovative sustainability assessments

Benefits

Working with RSB offers the opportunity to contribute to a globally recognised organisation at the forefront of sustainability and systems transformation.

·       Meaningful, mission-driven work: Contribute to advancing sustainability standards and real-world impact across global value chains, influencing how industries operate and evolve.

·       Flexible, high-impact assignments: Participate in intellectually engaging, project-based work that allows you to apply your expertise to real-world challenges.

·       Opportunity for ongoing collaboration: Consultants on the roster may be engaged on multiple assignments, fostering longer-term professional relationships with RSB.

______________________________________

Submission deadline: 24 October 2026

Type of Engagement: Project-based (as required) with an overarching Framework Agreement

Preferred Provider Type: Independent consultants and individuals, firms, agencies, and established organisations.

Remuneration: Agreed day rate

Location: Remote

Framework Agreement Duration: Until September 2028 [2 years], unless a Consultant or RSB request removal or changes to Framework Agreement.

Working Hours / Time Zone: CET ±4 hours time-zone compatibility, unless otherwise agreed for a specific assignment (minimum 4 hours per day overlapping with CET working hours).

Roster Launch: November 2026

_________________________________________

Diversity & Inclusion

RSB is committed to fostering diversity and inclusion across all its work. We strongly encourage expressions of interest from individuals and firms representing underrepresented groups, including, but not limited to, women, persons from the Global South, persons with disabilities, and members of other historically marginalised communities. We believe that diverse perspectives strengthen the quality and relevance of our work.

Conflict of Interest

Applicants must disclose any actual, potential, or perceived conflict of interest at the time of expression of interest and throughout the engagement. A conflict of interest exists where the Consultant has personal, professional, or financial relationships that could impair objectivity or create unfair advantage.

Anti-Corruption & Integrity

RSB operates a zero-tolerance policy with respect to fraud, bribery, corruption, and any other form of misconduct. All Consultants are expected to adhere to the highest ethical standards and to comply with applicable anti-corruption laws. Any breach may result in immediate termination and referral to relevant authorities.

How to Submit Your Expression of Interest

To be considered for inclusion on the RSB External Consultant Roster, Consultants should submit the following:

- Please fill out the complete questionnaire within this call for expression of interest

- A company capability statement (for firms/agencies) or a current curriculum vitae (for individuals), including a description of experience in similar assignments.

Later in the submission process. RSB will request further information to confirm shortlisted Consultants as trusted providers as part of our due diligence process:

•    Firms / organisations (and their employees): Tax identification and proof of registration

•    Self-employed individuals: Proof of independent status by registration with the relevant tax authority in the country of tax residence.

Several consultant types are listed separately on our website. You are welcome to submit expressionf of interest to multiple listings if you meet the respective requirements.

title: Platform Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
What we are building

ecoplanet builds the operating system for the energy transition. Our software helps European businesses cut energy costs, run more efficiently, and take the pain out of managing energy day to day. We are around 40 people and backed by EQT Ventures, HV Capital and others.


Why This Role Matters

You build and run the platform the whole product sits on: the event streams, the backend services and the cloud infrastructure everything else is built on. Meter readings arrive from industrial sites across Europe, through messages or us accessing APIs. Your job is to make sure that traffic lands reliably, moves through the system in a shape other teams can build on, and keeps doing so as the number of sites grows.
You join a team of 12 engineers in two squads. Small team, real ownership, and what you build reaches customers in weeks rather than quarters.

What you will work on

  • Event streaming. Kafka is the spine of the system. You own topic and schema design, partitioning, retention and delivery semantics  and the everyday reality behind them: consumers falling behind, replays, backfills, late and duplicated readings.
  • Backend services in TypeScript. The ingestion services, integrations and APIs around that stream. Every site is a little different, so a good part of the job is turning that variety into one consistent interface the product squads can rely on.
  • Cloud infrastructure on GCP. Compute, networking, IAM, infrastructure as code, CI/CD and observability. The goal is a paved road: other engineers ship and debug their own services without going through you.
  • Technical direction. You are senior enough to set it. Where we invest in the platform, what we standardise, what we deliberately leave rough for now  and bringing the rest of the team along with it.


What Sets You Up for Success

Must have:

  • At least 6–8 years building and running backend systems in production, including real time in a platform or infrastructure role that other engineers depended on
  • Strong backend engineering in TypeScript. You have designed, shipped and operated services and APIs in it — not just touched it around the edges of a frontend
  • Hands-on with Kafka in production. Topic design, consumer groups, ordering and delivery guarantees, and what you actually do at 3am when a consumer group is hours behind. A comparable streaming platform is fine if you know it at that depth
  • Solid on GCP or an equivalent cloud: containers, networking and IAM basics, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, monitoring and alerting. You have owned infrastructure, not just deployed onto it
  • Comfortable with high-volume time-series data: ingestion, data quality, backfills, and the everyday reality of late, missing and duplicated readings
  • You have seen a few things. Enough production years behind you to know which trade-offs come back to bite, when the boring option is the right one, and how to make a call with incomplete information instead of waiting for certainty
  • Kubernetes knowledge at the level of running it, not only deploying to it.
  • Clear written and spoken English. German is a plus
Nice to have:
  • Energy, industrial, IoT or another domain where the data comes off real hardware
  • Metering or device protocols, telemetry at scale, or streaming pipelines
  • Knowledge of a second programming language, like Python, Go or Kotlin
  • You run what you build: monitoring, alerting, and the occasional early morning debugging a pipeline


What You Get

  • Top-of-market team, flat hierarchy — work alongside people who push you to get better
  • Competitive salary
  • Full ownership from day one — you actively shape our company
  • Central office, easy commute — free lunch every Tuesday and Thursday
  • Wellpass membership

  • Real impact — your work supports Europe's transition to a smarter energy system

Your profile

B. in Operations, BizOps oder Founder's Office eines Scale-ups, als Gründer oder nach einem Start in Beratung, PE oder VC mit Wechsel ins Operative. Du hast Operations nachweislich auf- oder umgebaut, nicht nur analysiert.

title: Junior Talent Acquisition Partner (m/w/d)
description:
Davon träumen wir:

Mehr als Recruiting. Die richtigen Menschen für die richtigen Aufgaben.
 
VielfaltMenü befindet sich in einer Phase der Weiterentwicklung. Wir schärfen unsere Organisation, professionalisieren unsere Prozesse und richten uns noch konsequenter auf unsere Kund:innen, unsere Mitarbeiter:innen und nachhaltiges Wachstum aus.
Dazu gehört auch ein neues Verständnis von Recruiting.
Wir wollen Stellen nicht einfach besetzen. Wir wollen verstehen, welche Kompetenzen wir wirklich benötigen, wie wir sie erkennen und welche Menschen zu unserer Organisation und unseren Zielen passen.

Dafür suchen wir dich als Junior Talent Acquisition Partner:in

Du musst nicht bereits zehn Jahre Recruiting-Erfahrung mitbringen. 
Entscheidend sind für uns analytisches Denken, Neugier, ein ausgeprägter Qualitätsanspruch und die Fähigkeit, Menschen und Kompetenzen gut einzuschätzen.
  
Deine Aufgaben
Du begleitest Recruitingprozesse von der ersten Anforderungsanalyse bis zum unterschriebenen Arbeitsvertrag und entwickelst gemeinsam mit People & Culture unsere Recruitingstandards weiter.
Dabei arbeitest du eng mit unseren Führungskräften und der Geschäftsführung zusammen.
Talent Acquisition & Beratung
Du führst strukturierte Briefings mit Führungskräften und übersetzt Anforderungen in klare Kompetenz- und Kandidatenprofile.
Du berätst Führungskräfte bei der Auswahl geeigneter Kandidat:innen und sprichst auch dann eine klare Empfehlung aus, wenn die einfachste Lösung nicht die beste ist.
Interviews führst du eigenständig – vom operativen Recruiting bis hin zu Gesprächen auf Managementebene.
Kompetenzorientierte Auswahl
Wir wollen Auswahlentscheidungen stärker auf Kompetenzen und nachvollziehbare Kriterien stützen.
Du entwickelst strukturierte Interviewleitfäden, Bewertungsmatrizen und Auswahlstandards und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Entscheidungen vergleichbarer und belastbarer werden.
Bei diagnostischen Auswahlverfahren und Assessments begleitest du Konzeption, Durchführung und Auswertung.
Dein Anspruch dabei: weniger Bauchgefühl, mehr Qualität in der Entscheidung.
Candidate Experience & Kreativität
Professionelle Prozesse dürfen trotzdem persönlich sein.
Du entwickelst Ideen, wie wir Kandidat:innen besser erreichen und ihnen vom ersten Kontakt bis zur Einstellung eine überzeugende Candidate Experience bieten.
Dabei probierst du neue Recruitingwege aus, hinterfragst bestehende Prozesse und entwickelst gemeinsam mit uns moderne Recruitingformate.
Vertragsmanagement & Prozesse
Du steuerst den Recruitingprozess zuverlässig bis zum Vertragsabschluss.
Du bereitest Vertragsangebote vor, koordinierst Abstimmungen und sorgst dafür, dass Vereinbarungen vollständig, korrekt und termingerecht umgesetzt werden.
Arbeitsrechtliche und datenschutzrechtliche Fragestellungen erkennst du und kannst sie gemeinsam mit People & Culture bzw. unserer juristischen Expertise einordnen.
Du arbeitest strukturiert, standardisiert und detailgenau – ohne dabei unnötige Bürokratie aufzubauen.
 
Was du mitbringst
Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium, beispielsweise in Wirtschaftspsychologie, Psychologie, Personalmanagement, Wirtschafts- oder Rechtswissenschaften, oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.
Erste praktische Erfahrung im Recruiting, Talent Acquisition, HR oder in der Personalauswahl ist hilfreich – beispielsweise durch Werkstudententätigkeiten, Praktika oder deine erste berufliche Station.
Auch wenn du am Anfang deiner Karriere stehst, freuen wir uns ausdrücklich auf deine Bewerbung.
Wichtiger als die Anzahl deiner Berufsjahre ist für uns, wie du denkst und arbeitest.
Du hast Interesse an eignungsdiagnostischen und kompetenzorientierten Auswahlverfahren.
Du kannst Gespräche strukturieren, genau zuhören, kritisch nachfragen und deine Einschätzung anschließend nachvollziehbar begründen.
Du hast ein gutes Verständnis für wirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge und keine Scheu davor, mit Führungskräften und Geschäftsführung auf Augenhöhe zu diskutieren.
Juristische Fragestellungen – insbesondere rund um Arbeitsverträge und Arbeitsrecht – schrecken dich nicht ab. Idealerweise bringst du bereits entsprechende Grundkenntnisse mit.
Du arbeitest sehr sorgfältig und hast gleichzeitig Freude daran, Dinge neu zu denken.
 

Was uns bei dir besonders wichtig ist
Kreativität. 
Du akzeptierst nicht automatisch, dass Recruiting so funktionieren muss, wie es schon immer funktioniert hat.
Struktur. 
Du glaubst an Standards, klare Prozesse und nachvollziehbare Entscheidungen.
Detailorientierung.  
Ein falsches Datum im Arbeitsvertrag ist für dich keine Kleinigkeit.
Urteilsvermögen.
Du möchtest verstehen, welche Kompetenzen jemand wirklich mitbringt – und nicht nur, wie gut sich jemand präsentieren kann.
Mut zur Empfehlung.
Von dir erwarten wir nicht nur Organisation. Wir wollen deine Einschätzung hören.
Neugier.
Du möchtest verstehen, wie unser Geschäft funktioniert und was unsere Führungskräfte und Teams erfolgreich macht.
 

Was dich bei VielfaltMenü erwartet
VielfaltMenü steht für „Mehr als gutes Essen.“
Wir versorgen täglich Menschen in Bildungseinrichtungen und entwickeln uns als Unternehmen kontinuierlich weiter. People & Culture soll dabei nicht nur verwalten, sondern die Entwicklung des Unternehmens aktiv unterstützen. Du bekommst deshalb die Möglichkeit, unser Recruiting nicht nur auszuführen, sondern mitzugestalten. Du arbeitest eng mit Führungskräften, dem People & Culture-Team sowie der Geschäftsführung zusammen und erhältst früh Verantwortung für eigene Recruitingprozesse. Gleichzeitig geben wir dir Raum, dich fachlich weiterzuentwickeln.
In deiner Rolle genießt du echten Gestaltungsspielraum: Du baust moderne Qualitäts- sowie Prozessstrukturen aktiv mit auf und prägst die Standards eines führenden Unternehmens für Kita- und Schulverpflegung in Deutschland. Dabei profitierst du von kurzen Entscheidungswegen und einer Geschäftsführung, die Qualität strategisch fördert.
Neben einem unbefristeten Arbeitsvertrag in einem zukunftssicheren Markt erwarten dich eine attraktive, transparente Vergütung sowie klare Entwicklungsperspektiven durch strukturierte Einarbeitung und individuelle Weiterbildungen. Wir unterstützen deine Work-Life-Balance durch 30 Urlaubstage, geregelte Arbeitszeiten und die Möglichkeit zum mobilen Arbeiten. Zudem erhältst du moderne Arbeitsmittel inklusive Diensthandy. Eine gute ÖPNV-Anbindung und ein engagiertes, kollegiales Team runden unser Angebot ab.
 

Klingt nach dir?
Dann interessiert uns nicht nur dein Lebenslauf.
Wir möchten wissen, wie du über Menschen, Kompetenzen und gute Personalauswahl denkst.
Bewirb dich bei uns und gestalte gemeinsam mit uns, wie Recruiting bei VielfaltMenü künftig funktioniert.
 
VielfaltMenü – Mehr als gutes Essen.

title: Data Platform & Data Architecture Consultant
description:
About the role

As a Data Platform & Data Architecture Consultant, you are the person clients trust to turn their data infrastructure from a bottleneck into a competitive advantage. You design data landscapes, stand up and scale cloud data platforms, and set the guardrails that let entire organisations build on data safely and efficiently.

Our consultants bring varied paths and perspectives to this work. What unites them is structural thinking, a drive to understand the business context behind every technical decision, and the ability to operate across both the blueprint and the build. Across engagements, you may operate as a data architect, lead a platform build, or contribute at the strategic advisory level, often blending several of these roles within a single engagement.

 

What the work looks like

Building and operating platforms. You design, provision, and harden cloud data platforms end to end, covering storage and compute, networking, security and IAM, observability, and cost. You codify infrastructure using tools like Terraform, Pulumi, or CloudFormation and establish governance frameworks such as data catalogs, data contracts, RBAC models, and SLAs that let organisations scale data access without losing control. You build platforms that multiple teams and business domains can rely on, not just at launch, but as they grow.

Shaping the data architecture. You design logical and physical data models, map data flows and lineage across systems, and make the structural decisions that determine how data is organised, integrated, and consumed. This can mean designing a target-state architecture for a client migrating from legacy systems to a modern cloud lakehouse, or defining domain boundaries and data product interfaces in a data mesh adoption.

Advising and translating. You sit at the intersection of technology and business. You work with data engineers, data scientists, product owners, and senior client stakeholders to understand what they need, then turn that into platform strategy and architecture decisions. You are the person a CTO trusts to make the right call on how their data infrastructure should evolve.


Minimum Qualifications
  • Master’s Degree in Engineering or Technology (e.g., Computer Science, Data Engineering, Information Systems, or similar) 
  • Verbal and written fluency in English
  • 2–4 years of full-time work experience in cloud data infrastructure, data platform engineering, or data architecture. Experience working in agile product or delivery teams, gained after completing your Master's degree
  • Strong hands-on experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including compute, storage, networking, and identity management
  • Practical experience with at least one modern cloud data platform such as Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, or Microsoft Fabric

About the role

Gauss Fusion is aiming to build the first commercial scale fusion power plant based on the stellarator concept and is seeking an experienced mechanical engineer to lead on development of the robotic maintenance approach.
The fusion environment within the reactor is very aggressive, and in-vessel components such as the breeder blanket and divertor will need to be replaced on a regular basis as the materials become damaged by the radiation. Due to the environment inside the device, and in order to maintain a high overall availability, the maintenance must be done robotically using automated systems to extract and replace the components and bring the removed ones to a hot cell for separation, waste treatment, and recycling.
Gauss Fusion is looking for an innovative mechanical design engineer with experience in robotics to lead the work defining and developing the maintenance approach for the Gauss stellarator power plant and its key stellarator systems. While the magnetic configuration will be designed to maximise access to the reactor, the complex geometry poses a challenge to fixations and kinematics, and inventive approaches to the problem are required.


Main responsibilities

Manage the Gauss Fusion maintenance approach to meet the requirements of a commercial scale fusion power plant design:

  • Develop workable approaches to achieving high power plant availability, taking account of engineering and physics requirements across the reactor.
  • Integrate these remote maintenance requirements into plant layout specifications.
  • Define approaches to minimising hot cell inventory through efficient handling of removed components.
  • Lead development of the breeder blanket and divertor segmentation and fixations resulting from these approaches.
  • Lead development of remote maintenance testing and demonstration systems for the reactor.


Qualification and educational requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or related field, master’s or Ph.D. preferred.
  • Technical experience: 
    • Minimum of 6 years of experience in mechanical engineering, preferably in large-scale engineering projects.
    • Experience in designing complex mechanical systems, preferably in the energy or nuclear industry.
    • Familiarity with CAD software and engineering analysis tools.


Competences and preferred skills

  • Experience developing remote maintenance systems operating in hazardous environments
  • Strong background in mechatronics, motion control and mechanical integration. 
  • Experience with digital mock-up will be an asset
  • Familiarity with maintenance, inspection and intervention systems 
  • Familiarity with system engineering processes, requirements management and verification activities. Strong understanding of mechanical design principles and engineering mechanics.
  • Proficiency in structural analysis, finite element analysis (FEA), and kinematic analysis.
  • Ability to manage multidisciplinary teams and coordinate with other engineering disciplines.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

title: Solutions Architect f/m/d
description:
Apaleo is the world's most open, API-first property management platform powering the next generation of hospitality operations. Its modular, AI-powered infrastructure enables hoteliers to customise their tech stack, automate routine work, and deliver seamless, personalised guest experiences, powered by best-in-class apps and autonomous AI agents that adapt to every stay.

Why this role

You are the technical voice in front of strategic customers, at a moment when hospitality is being rebuilt around AI. We are launching our own AI agent platform, and we need architects who can show operators what comes next.

  • High trust. You own the technical answer in front of strategic customers and deals.
  • High visibility. Your work shows up in deals, key accounts and customer stories, and it reaches Product.
  • High freedom. You decide how to solve a problem, which tools to use and what to prototype.
  • Fast iteration. We test ideas within days, try new technology early and share what works.

Your mission

Win and grow strategic accounts with technical credibility, and turn what you learn in the field into input for the product. You look at a customer's current architecture and show how an Apaleo-centred setup delivers their goals. You also help them put AI agents to work, deciding what should be an agent, what it costs and how to set it up. Sales and Account Management own the relationship and the commercial terms. You own the technical answer.

What you will do

  • Technical discovery and solution scoping. Lead discovery where a standard demo is not enough. Write clear scopes covering what Apaleo delivers natively, what needs a short-term solution and what is out of scope.
  • Proofs of concept. Build fast, working proofs of concept (quick demos that show technical fit). Agree scope in writing first, and build in a safe test environment, never with live guest data.
  • Agents and automations. Design and build agents and automations for customer use cases, using n8n or Make today and Apaleo's own AI agent platform as it launches. Write code where agents need deterministic steps.
  • Hands-on delivery and short-term solutions. Work alongside the customer, building only where it unblocks a named deal, removes an adoption risk or fills a product gap. Agree an exit plan (an end date, a replacement and a named owner) before you start.
  • Post-sale health checks and expansions. Diagnose gaps against the go-live specification, run proactive checks (for example 90 days after go-live) and scope integrations for expanding customers.
  • Reusable assets. Turn every engagement into a reference architecture, pattern or template that the next twenty customers can use.
  • Thought leadership. Join prospect and customer conversations on how AI will change hospitality over the next two to three years.
  • Product feedback. Test new technology on real customer problems. Share prototypes and field evidence with Product, ending every experiment with a clear decision: adopt, hand over or drop.

How you work

  • You decide the approach, the stack and the order of work.
  • You protect three guardrails: written scope before a proof of concept, an exit plan before a custom build and no commercial promises.
  • You go from idea to prototype in days and show it early.
  • You think in systems and build for reuse, not one-off projects.
  • You share findings openly with Sales, Account Management and Product.

Who you work with

Sales/BD and Account Management (they call you in at defined deal triggers), Customer Success, Product, Security, Partnerships, RevOps and Senior Leadership. 

What you bring

Must have

  • Multiple years in solution architecture, solution engineering or technical consulting in B2B SaaS, ideally with complex software such as ERP or enterprise platforms
  • Strong API skills: REST, authentication, webhooks and events, and data-flow design
  • Hands-on workflow automation (n8n preferred) and practical experience building with LLM agents
  • A systems thinker with real AI curiosity, who uses AI tools day to day
  • Stakeholder management experience and credibility with executives and IT teams
  • Self-direction, an ownership mindset and the discipline to say no to scope that does not advance a deal
  • Curiosity that ends in working prototypes, not just opinions
  • Clear, structured documentation habits
  • Fluent English and German skills
  • Willingness to travel, including regularly to France and the UK

Strong plus

  • Hospitality or travel experience, including hotel operations and PMS concepts (reservations, folios, rate plans, night audit)
  • Experience with another cloud PMS, channel manager or payments integrations
  • Enterprise architecture experience on large, multi-site projects
  • Applied AI or ML background, or experience with MCP and agent platforms
  • SQL and BI fundamentals

How we measure success

  • Architecture engagements and blueprints delivered each quarter
  • Customer satisfaction with your contribution
  • Adoption of recommended apps, integrations and agents
  • Share of engagements served by an existing reusable pattern
  • Revenue impact e.g. deal unblocked, AI adoption, or churn averted

Your first 90 days

  • Days 1 to 30: Learn the platform and ways of working, shadow discovery and proof of concept work, and take over open customer projects.
  • Days 31 to 60: Lead technical discovery on live deals and run your first health check with Account Management.
  • Days 61 to 90: Deliver a proof of concept or short-term solution end to end with an exit plan, and share your first experiment with Product.

 

What We Offer

Culture & Growth

  • A Diverse & International Team: Work alongside passionate professionals from over 20 nationalities, bringing unique cultural perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences to shape the future of hospitality tech.
  • Growth & Development: As we scale, so do your opportunities. You'll benefit from 360° feedback reviews, a dedicated learning budget, and plenty of chances to take on more responsibility. Our evolving career framework ensures you have increasing opportunities to learn new skills, advance your career, and make an impact.
  • Autonomy & Ownership: Great ideas can come from anywhere. We empower you to take responsibility, make decisions, and contribute directly in an environment built on trust, transparency, and collaboration.
  • Shape the Future of Hospitality Tech: Be part of a fast-growing scale-up transforming the hospitality industry. From day one, your work drives real impact and you'll have the freedom to bring your ideas to life.
  • Competitive & Fair Compensation: We believe great work deserves great pay. Our salaries are competitive and guided by benchmarking data to ensure fairness across all roles and teams. We make sure to recognize and reward performance and contribution.

Perks & Lifestyle

  • Flexible & Remote Work Options: We focus on results, not clocking hours. You can work from home, the office or in a hybrid setup, with flexibility to adapt your schedule as long as it makes sense for your role, your team and our business.
  • Free Public Transport: Travel across Germany with ease using our fully covered Deutschland Ticket.
  • Team Connection: Strong connections fuel collaboration. We celebrate and connect through regular team dinners, company meetups, Oktoberfest celebrations, Christmas parties, and other offsite events.
  • Paid Time Off: Enjoy 30 days of vacation to fully disconnect, recharge, and return inspired.
  • Health & Wellbeing: Prioritize your health with access to hundreds of gyms, fitness studios, and wellness options through our EGYM Wellpass membership.

How you make an impact joining Apaleo: Joining Apaleo means more than just taking on a role it's about driving real change in the hospitality industry. Your contributions will directly shape our innovative platform, influence company-wide decisions, and help redefine the future of hospitality tech. At Apaleo, your voice matters, your ideas are valued, and your impact is tangible. Be part of a team where your work fuels progress, collaboration sparks innovation, and growth is a shared journey.

We celebrate differences and believe that diversity enriches our team and drives innovation.

Wie oft im Leben bekommt man die Chance, Enterprise Architecture nicht zu reparieren, sondern von null aufzubauen? 

Die meisten EAM-Rollen beginnen mit einem Erbe: ein Tool, das vor Jahren jemand anderes gekauft hat, ein Repository mit Stand von vorgestern, eine Community, die sich aus Pflicht trifft. Diese Rolle beginnt mit einem leeren Blatt.

Tool-Auswahl, Metamodell, Governance: nichts davon ist entschieden. Das wird deine Entscheidung. Solche Konstellationen gibt es selten und sie halten nicht lange. Worum es geht 
Enterprise Architecture scheitert selten an fehlenden Frameworks. Sie scheitert daran, dass niemand das Repository pflegt, das Tool nicht mit den Quellsystemen spricht und die Architektur-Community nach dem dritten Meeting einschläft. Diese Rolle verhindert genau das. Du baust die Grundlage, auf der EAM in diesem Konzern funktioniert. Prozesse, die Menschen tatsächlich befolgen. Deine Aufgaben

  • Du definierst, wie Architekturarbeit im Konzern abläuft: Prozessmodelle, Rollen und Verantwortlichkeiten, Beschreibungen und Anforderungskataloge.
  • Du wählst das EAM-Tool aus, von der Marktsondierung über die Ausschreibung bis zur Entscheidung, und verantwortest danach Implementierung und Konfiguration.
  • Du konzipierst die Anbindung an Konfigurationsdatenbank, Service-Management und Cloud-Umgebungen, damit das Repository aktuell bleibt, ohne dass jemand es manuell nachführt.
  • Du entwickelst das Architektur-Metamodell weiter, wenn Geschäft oder Technologie es verlangen und misst die Reife der Prozesse regelmäßig gegen Industriestandards.
  • Du probierst neue Methoden aus, etwa Capability Maps oder Wertstromanalysen, und entscheidest, was davon in diesen Konzern passt.
  • Du sorgst für Betrieb und Skalierbarkeit der Plattform, inklusive Rollen und Zugriffskonzepten und definierst Kennzahlen für Datenqualität.

Dein Profil

Gynaecological care the way it's supposed to be: Personalised, easy to reach, effective.

Women are diagnosed on average four years later than men, across 770 different diseases. They spend 25 % more of their lives in poor health. That is the gender health gap, and science says two things keep it open: too little access to specialists in women's health, and far too little research on women in the first place.

femote works on both.

Step One: we turn ordinary statutory gynaecological practices into digital care champions. So that the specialists we do have can care for more patients properly, within the resources they are given.

Step Two: we turn generalist doctors into specialists by equipping them with clinical diagnostic and decision support built specifically for women's health, trained on data collected by Step One.

Where we stand

  • Supported by leaders of the German gynaecological medical associations
  • Backed by industry angels from pharmaceuticals and medical publishing
  • Innovation grant secured from the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy
  • Part of the Lausitz Model Region, giving us deep integration into the statutory system and reach to women regardless of their spending power
  • MVP in pilot phase with real practices (Stack: Flutter, Supabase, Postgres. Up for debate once you join)
  • Pre-seed stage, with funding in place to bring you on

Tasks

We are looking for our first engineer to build femote's product and shape the technical foundation it grows on.

As our founding engineer, you will build our first SaaS product, a patient app and a professional interface, under European General Product Safety Regulation guidelines in the first year while we prepare for medical device certification in year two.

Every case we capture is structured so it can carry clinical evidence later, which is what makes algorithmic and decision-support features possible at all. You will not build those alone, but you need to direct that work, and the architecture that makes it possible has to be laid now.

Requirements

We value smartness, humility and the ability to learn and adapt quickly over hard skills on paper. Please apply, even if you don't tick all the boxes.

What you have done

  • Experience running a SaaS product from building to shipping to operating in production
  • Strong data modelling and processing, including consent, provenance and pseudonymisation, so captured data can lawfully support clinical evidence and model training later
  • Bonus: experience building algorithmic or AI-enabled features
  • Bonus: experience building in a regulated field (MDR, AI Act, or similar)
  • Bonus: German speaking, though not required

How you work

  • You ship fast without lowering the bar. Short iteration cycles and pragmatic solutions, with engineering practices solid enough to stand up to a notified body.
  • You set the pattern, not just the code. Everything the first engineer does becomes the default for everyone after. You write it down, you teach it, and you build with that in mind.
  • You do not think in taboos. You will be reading about discharge, bleeding and pelvic pain at nine in the morning and building interfaces for it. If that is awkward for you, this is not your role.
  • You want to understand why we are doing this in gynaecology. You do not have to arrive as an expert in women's health, and we are happy to offer a steep learning curve. The curiosity has to be yours.
  • You are reflective. You take feedback without putting armour on, and you say when you are stuck rather than when it is already too late.

Benefits

  • Meaningful equity as hurdle shares or an instrument with equivalent tax treatment.
  • Genuine ownership of the technical direction
  • Full-time, with flexible working hours
  • Room to grow into the CTO role: owning medical device certification, security and data handling, the engineering team you hire around you, and representing femote's technical direction to regulators, partners and investors.

Our hiring process

  1. Conversation with Frederike (45 min): what we are building, what you have built, and whether this is the right fit for both sides.
  2. Meet the team: Tabea and Insa, the people you will work with every day.
  3. Technical deep dive with one of our technical advisors: architecture, data modelling and how you would approach our product.
  4. Offer.

From application to offer takes no longer than six weeks.

Who you will work with

We are a small team, and between us we have treated patients, built data infrastructure and products for enterprise clients, and studied how health systems fail people at scale.

Our team is technical enough that you don't have to translate engineering reality into business language.

Frederike Kugland, Founder: Quit her job for yeast infections. Built a company around it.
WHU graduate turned developer. Ex-Managing Partner at tech consultancy Pandata. Learned to code because she hated Excel, now runs product, fundraising and sales. Technical enough to be your sparring partner but too busy to interfere with your work. Doesn't shy away from founder-led marketing, discussing her intimate health on the Gyncast Podcast.

Dr. med. Tabea Siebler, Medical Lead: Doctor. Polyglot. One exam room isn't enough for her.
Certified gynaecologist, speaks 6 languages, not as a Duolingo streak but to serve her patients. Implemented a new consultation hour for Female Genital Mutilation and Cutting at her last clinic. Currently studying Public Health at the London School of Hygiene because treating one patient at a time wasn't enough.

Insa Deden, Software Development: Left the ward to build what was missing on it.
Trained and worked as a registered nurse in anaesthesia at University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf, then went to study health information management to work on the problems she had been living with every shift. She brings the care-delivery perspective that sits next to Tabea's clinical one: what it actually takes for software to hold up at scale in daily practice, rather than in a demo. Moving from working student to full-time.

Alongside them: a fractional CFO, regulatory and compliance support from the former Head of Regulatory at Heidelberg Engineering, and technical advisors.

About us

IGES GmbH specialises in health economic and strategic research and consulting services for international pharmaceutical and medical device manufacturers. It offers biotech, pharmaceutical and medical device companies solutions for market access, pricing and reimbursement of their medical innovations. The company has offices in France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and the United Kingdom and also provides support for multinational product launches. IGES is part of the Athagoras Group, which brings together various consulting firms for the life sciences industry.

To strengthen our team in the area of Value Strategy & RWE, we are looking for a Senior Consultant Real World Evidence - Focus on Healthcare Data Analysis (m/f/d)


Your mission

  • Design, execution, evaluation and interpretation of analyses based on claims data – in particular health insurance fund data (GKV) and/or registry data – from data preparation through cohort definition to the presentation of results 
  • Interpretation and contextualisation of analysis results to generate robust real-world evidence, and its translation into strategic recommendations for our clients
  • Strategic consulting for market access, HE&OR and RWE departments at leading pharmaceutical companies and emerging biotechs
  • Providing technical oversight and quality assurance for analyses in interdisciplinary projects, as well as mentoring less experienced colleagues
  • Providing support on HTA-related issues (e.g. evidence requirements, PICO scoping, analysis strategies) and translating the results into publications, presentations and project reports
  • Conducting systematic literature reviews and structured evaluations to supplement findings from claims data
  • Active involvement in the further development of internal data and methodological expertise for analyses of health data from the FDZ-Gesundheit
  • Collaboration on the preparation and publication of results, e.g. in scientific journals, project reports and presentations of findings


Your profile

  • Successfully completed degree (master's/diploma) in health services research, public health, health economics, statistics, epidemiology or a comparable field 
  • Several years’ relevant professional experience in the analysis of claims data – in particular health insurance fund data (GKV) and/or register data – in an industrial or academic environment
  • Demonstrable ability to interpret analysis results independently, synthesise them into real-world evidence and present them in a manner tailored to the target audience
  • Proficiency in epidemiological and statistical methods, to the extent required for the practical evaluation of claims data
  • Experience in drafting scientific documents, e.g. study protocols, study reports or publications
  • Programming skills in R or Python would be an advantage
  • Knowledge of HTA/market access requirements is welcome but not essential
  • Analytical thinking, structured and careful working style, and a high degree of initiative
  • Open-minded and communicative personality with a team- and client-oriented approach
  • Fluent written and spoken German and English (academic level)


Our offer

  • Collaboration on varied projects involving highly innovative drugs at the interface of healthcare research, real-world evidence and strategic consulting
  • An interdisciplinary, collegial working environment with flat hierarchies, short decision-making paths and good development prospects
  • Professional and personal development through challenging project work, plenty of scope for your own ideas and individually tailored further training (e.g. conferences)
  • Gain practical experience in using large claims data sets, as well as early development of expertise relating to the FDZ Gesundheit
  • Flexible working arrangements after structured training at the Berlin site, including the option to work from home
  • A Permanent position with competitive remuneration, flexible working hours, 30 days of holiday and additional time off on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve

title: Senior Analytics Engineer
description:
As our Senior Analytics Engineer for Operations, you'll own that data end to end, the model behind it, the metrics it produces, and the trust the business places in both.

This role isn't just "build the metric, ship the dashboard." We want someone who looks past the number to the process behind it, where it's manual, where it's fragile, where the right tool removes the work instead of just reporting on it. You'll have a direct line to influencing how those processes and the surrounding product actually work, not just how they're measured.

You'll sit embedded inside Operations, partnering with the TRI (Trust & Risk Intelligence) domain wherever the two overlap, while working inside the Data & Analytics team's AE guild — so you'll have the tools and the context to actually contribute, not just execute.

What You Will Be Doing

Own the Operations data model — reconciliation, treasury, payments, lifecycle, and onboarding — turning raw operational events into documented, trustworthy data products on the DWH
Partner directly with Operations stakeholders on day-to-day questions, ad hoc requests, and recurring reporting, acting as their primary data point of contact — while pushing routine, repeatable questions toward self-service instead of answering the same thing by hand every time
Look past the metric to the process behind it — understand how everything actually works end to end, spot where manual effort or fragile handoffs are the real problem, and identify which tools (not just which query) would solve it
Define and maintain key metrics for reconciliation accuracy, treasury positions, payment success/failure rates, and onboarding conversion, working within the team's central metric architecture
Participate in data quality and governance practices for the domain
Bring process and product ideas to the table directly — you're close enough to the operational reality to see what should change, and this role expects you to say so and help make it happen, not just report the numbers upward
Your First Six Months

First month Learn the Operations domain and how it currently works and reports, end to end. Meet your stakeholders and your teammates. Ship a first small, well-scoped fix or data product from the existing backlog to get real signal into the system quickly

First 3 months Own at least one Operations sub-domain's metrics end to end. Start contributing to the shared Risk/TRI conversations, and bring your first concrete process or tooling suggestion to a stakeholder — something you noticed while getting close to the actual workflow

First 6 months Operations stakeholders treat you as their data partner, not the new person. Routine checks are answered by self-service — what reaches you is what actually needs a person. You hold real, independent ownership over the data and workflows under your supervision

Who You Are


You've worked as an analytics engineer or senior analyst on technical projects involving data modeling on a modern data platform (Databricks, Spark, or dbt) — not just querying data others built
You write excellent SQL for analytical work, and you can pick up Python for anything SQL doesn't cover well
You're confident gathering requirements directly from operational stakeholders and turning ambiguous asks into clean, documented metrics
You default to precision over speed when the two are in tension — Operations data feeds regulatory and financial reporting, and being wrong quietly is worse than being slow

You think past the metric to the process it describes — you want to understand how the domain's tasks actually get done, spot which tool or automation would remove real work rather than just report on it, and you push for that change rather than waiting to be asked
You have a high level of autonomy and self-direction — you're the one who decides what needs fixing, not just how to measure it
AI-assisted workflows and tools are just part of how you work, not a novelty

Background in banking, fintech, treasury, or payments operations
Experience working across multiple stakeholder groups with overlapping but not identical needs

title: Senior Analytics Engineer
description:
As our Senior Analytics Engineer for Operations, you'll own that data end to end, the model behind it, the metrics it produces, and the trust the business places in both.

This role isn't just "build the metric, ship the dashboard." We want someone who looks past the number to the process behind it, where it's manual, where it's fragile, where the right tool removes the work instead of just reporting on it. You'll have a direct line to influencing how those processes and the surrounding product actually work, not just how they're measured.

You'll sit embedded inside Operations, partnering with the TRI (Trust & Risk Intelligence) domain wherever the two overlap, while working inside the Data & Analytics team's AE guild — so you'll have the tools and the context to actually contribute, not just execute.

What You Will Be Doing

Own the Operations data model — reconciliation, treasury, payments, lifecycle, and onboarding — turning raw operational events into documented, trustworthy data products on the DWH
Partner directly with Operations stakeholders on day-to-day questions, ad hoc requests, and recurring reporting, acting as their primary data point of contact — while pushing routine, repeatable questions toward self-service instead of answering the same thing by hand every time
Look past the metric to the process behind it — understand how everything actually works end to end, spot where manual effort or fragile handoffs are the real problem, and identify which tools (not just which query) would solve it
Define and maintain key metrics for reconciliation accuracy, treasury positions, payment success/failure rates, and onboarding conversion, working within the team's central metric architecture
Participate in data quality and governance practices for the domain
Bring process and product ideas to the table directly — you're close enough to the operational reality to see what should change, and this role expects you to say so and help make it happen, not just report the numbers upward
Your First Six Months

First month Learn the Operations domain and how it currently works and reports, end to end. Meet your stakeholders and your teammates. Ship a first small, well-scoped fix or data product from the existing backlog to get real signal into the system quickly

First 3 months Own at least one Operations sub-domain's metrics end to end. Start contributing to the shared Risk/TRI conversations, and bring your first concrete process or tooling suggestion to a stakeholder — something you noticed while getting close to the actual workflow

First 6 months Operations stakeholders treat you as their data partner, not the new person. Routine checks are answered by self-service — what reaches you is what actually needs a person. You hold real, independent ownership over the data and workflows under your supervision

Who You Are


You've worked as an analytics engineer or senior analyst on technical projects involving data modeling on a modern data platform (Databricks, Spark, or dbt) — not just querying data others built
You write excellent SQL for analytical work, and you can pick up Python for anything SQL doesn't cover well
You're confident gathering requirements directly from operational stakeholders and turning ambiguous asks into clean, documented metrics
You default to precision over speed when the two are in tension — Operations data feeds regulatory and financial reporting, and being wrong quietly is worse than being slow
You can hold two stakeholders' definitions of "the same" metric and reconcile them, rather than picking whichever is more convenient
You think past the metric to the process it describes — you want to understand how the domain's tasks actually get done, spot which tool or automation would remove real work rather than just report on it, and you push for that change rather than waiting to be asked
You have a high level of autonomy and self-direction — you're the one who decides what needs fixing, not just how to measure it
AI-assisted workflows and tools are just part of how you work, not a novelty


Nice to Have


Background in banking, fintech, treasury, or payments operations
Experience working across multiple stakeholder groups with overlapping but not identical needs
Familiarity with regulatory or financial reporting data requirements
Occasional exposure to BI-layer reporting (PSM, lifecycle, or similar) when it intersects with your data products

Finom stands by you at every step, embodying our commitment to your well-being and success reflected in our modern, friendly, and eco-conscious corporate culture. We offer constant support and care to ensure your Finom experience is successful and fulfilling.

Automation. You develop our existing setup, and automate finance and administrative workflows wherever it adds value.

Portfolio monitoring. You collect the reporting from our 150+ portfolio companies and use AI to turn the data into insights that the team can act on.

Fund accounting and reporting. You review the work of our fund administrator and support the preparation of quarterly LP reports, annual financial statements and tax filings.
